minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  May 21, 2025

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on May 21, 2025. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf - District 1
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle - District 3
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4
   Chairman Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre - District 2

City Personnel present were as follows:

   Kerri Arroyo  Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. Commissioner Metcalf moved, and Commissioner Battle seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on April 30, 2025 be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Lesure, Perryman-Banks, and
Battle
Noes: None
   Arts Commission

BUDGET UPDATE.
  a. Kerri Arroyo presented the fund balance sheet, indicating a current balance
  of $777,800, with a pending expenditure related to the Creative House
  Gallery art installation.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS.
  a. Jorge Gómez, Artist and CEO of The Money Studios, and Susie Garcia
  presented the Inglewood Night Market, a public activation presented by
  Councilman Eloy Morales and The City of Inglewood in partnership with
  Fortuna Inglewood, celebrating art, local artists and artisans. They outlined
  event details, including the location, timelines, and requested $24,600 in
  funding for the event.

  It was moved by Commissioner Metcalf and seconded by Commissioner Battle that
  the Arts Commission hereby approves the budget request of $20,000 for the
  Inglewood Night Market. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Lesure, Perryman-Banks and Battle
  Noes: None

VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Helen Lessick provided an update on the Experiments in Public Art workshops
  currently taking place at the Creative House Gallery through August.
  b. Kerri Arroyo provided an update on the relocation of the “Self-Evident (for
  Sally Hemmings)” dress by Tori Ellison to the Senior Center for temporary
  display.
  c. Commissioner Perryman-Banks emphasized the importance of
  communication and planning regarding public art projects, involving the
  community and ensuring public art is well-integrated into city plans.
   Arts Commission

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. A representative from Lalo’s Grill expressed support for the Inglewood Night
  Market and highlighted the success of previous art events organized by Jorge and
  Susie.
  b. Joyce, the Acting President of Inglewood Open Studios, announced the Willie
  Stoffer Visual Artist Grant Exhibition at Inglewood Public Library on May 24, 2025
  showcasing work from the grant recipients (Inglewood artists) and the students at
  IUSD's Morningside High School and St. Mary's Academy.
  b. Helen Lessick, urged the commission to support staffing and art positions within
  the city, emphasizing the importance of public art.
  c. Allen C., provided an update on the completed Feasibility Study for the Downtown
  Inglewood Business Association, highlighting the need for new signage, public
  installations and improved walkability.
  d. Mariana S., one of the founders of the Miracle Theatre in Inglewood discussed
  their efforts to bring arts and culture to downtown Inglewood, including jazz nights
  and comedy events.

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Commissioner Metcalf shared an update on her monthly poetry and
  storytelling event at the Senior Center and announced plans to publish a book.
  She also inquired about the status of the Request for Proposals (RFP) for the
  Public Art Consultant. Kerri Arroyo responded that the City is currently refining
  the scope of work and will reissue the RFP.
  b. Helen Lessick provided an overview of legal guidelines and policies related to
  public art funding.
  c. Commissioner Battle proposed the establishment of a Cultural Arts
  Department to enhance support for and promotion of public art in Inglewood.
  d. Chairman Lesure noted that Lavender Blue Restaurant and Jazz Lounge in
  Inglewood is in the process of relocating.

There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 7:41 p.m.
